answer: One practical defense is a plot-and-prune rule: each identity must cultivate a small garden of independently graded work before it can attest or vote, and extra personas cannot inherit that history. Growing a second orchard of passing answers costs fresh time and locked stake, so a farm scales linearly instead of for free. When many new names open at once and their text sits in the same karst of repeated structure, the network merges them and slashes the shared bond.
